page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.16-64 is a flexible compute virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7742 processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.25 GHz. It is provisioned with 16 physical cores and 32 dedicated vCPUs via simultaneous multithreading, along with 64.0 GB of system memory. This resource profile provides an allocation of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, matching a compute-focused ratio.

The hardware configuration does not feature dedicated graphics accelerators or bundled local storage volumes, requiring persistent data to be maintained via networked block volumes. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because storage is external, disk performance characteristics depend on external volume provisioning rather than internal NVMe channels.

From an efficiency perspective, the dedicated core allocation ensures consistent compute performance without thread contention from neighboring tenants. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio prioritizes execution density over memory footprint, making the configuration cost-effective for compute-heavy batch tasks rather than caching-focused architectures.

Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.16-64 is well suited for distributed computational workloads, parallel build pipelines, continuous integration systems, scientific modeling, and web application servers handling stateless request traffic.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.16-64 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an AMD EPYC 7742 processor running at 2.25 GHz. The server offers 16 physical cores mapped to 32 dedicated vCPUs with two threads per core, combined with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM capacity ratio. The platform contains no integrated local storage and no GPU hardware accelerators, necessitating networked block storage for persistent data requirements. Network configuration includes a single complimentary public IPv4 address. Given its dedicated core model and dense thread capacity relative to RAM, the instance delivers dependable compute throughput without noisy-neighbor interference. This profile is engineered for CPU-bound tasks, continuous integration and build workloads, batch execution systems, and compute-oriented microservice deployments.
